BiblicalUsage: Daniel pleads, cause Thine ear to hear, O my God, and open Thine eyes: we do not present our supplications before Thee for our righteousnesses, but for Thy great mercies. The psalmist says, give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications; and out of the depths he cries, Lord, hear my voice, let Thine ears be attentive. And Zechariah promises a spirit of grace and of supplications, and they shall look upon Him whom they have pierced. The word is earnest prayer, supplication: the cry of a people who know they have nothing to bring but need.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that supplication is prayer at its most honest. I believe Daniel's ground is the only ground there is: not our righteousnesses, but His great mercies. And I hold that the spirit of supplication Zechariah promises ends where it must, looking on the One who was pierced.
